name: herdr-corral
description: Visual editor for herdr's config.toml. Corral your agents' layout, keys, and theme, then download the file.

paragraphs: corral is a static single-page app. Everything runs in the tab you have it open in: read a config file, edit it in memory against a live mock of herdr, and write the file back with every comment and untouched line byte-identical. Nothing is uploaded, there is no account, and there is no server — closing the tab is the only "logout" there is.

A corral is the pen where a scattered herd gets gathered and arranged, and "to corral" is exactly what this app does to a sprawling config.toml: take herdr's 167 settings, wherever they sit in the file, and lay them out somewhere you can see and reach every one of them. herdr herds coding agents inside your terminal; corral herds the file that tells it how to. The name follows the rest of the ecosystem's own convention — short, lowercase, one word.
